verdict.rationale: Restate itself can trigger handler code when events arrive. Handlers can be invoked through Kafka topics, any handler can serve as a durable webhook endpoint, and incoming events are persisted and processed exactly once. However, the trigger logic lives in developer-written handler code, not in user-definable rules, and the Kafka subscription mechanics are only thinly evidenced. Missing for 10: a declarative rule or condition definition for event-to-action mappings, detailed docs on event subscription setup and filtering, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can define rules that trigger actions automatically on events

citations.quote: There are three ways to invoke a handler: over HTTP, using typed clients, or through Kafka topics.
Restate eliminates this complexity by providing **lightweight, transactional event processing** with zero consumer management and built-in state.
Any handler can be a durable webhook endpoint. No need to do anything special or extra!
Restate persists all incoming events, and ensures that they are processed exactly once, across failures and restarts
